title: Optimality of Differential Bounds for Alzette's ARX Box
summary: The source gives round-dependent differential bounds for selecting Alzette's ARX box and leaves their optimality through five rounds at every offset to be proved or refuted.

formal_statement.body: For the iterated ARX-box structure used to select Alzette, a candidate must have differential bounds, measured as $-\log_2$ probabilities, of $0,1,2,6,$ and $10$ for $1,2,3,4,$ and $5$ rounds, respectively, at each of the four possible offsets. Prove or refute the conjecture that these bounds are optimal through five rounds for every offset.

scope.domain: Differential cryptanalysis of the iterated ARX-box structure used to select Alzette.
parameters: Round count: one through five rounds for the stated differential bounds
Offset: each of the four possible offsets
Differential bound: measured as negative base-2 log-probability
scope.unresolved_remainder: Whether the stated differential bounds are optimal through five rounds for every offset.

citations.label: Alzette: a 64-bit ARX-box (feat. CRAX and TRAX)

progress.summary: The source presents these bounds as a heuristic criterion for selecting the final Alzette ARX-box and explicitly conjectures that they are optimal through five rounds for all four offsets.
citation_labels: Christof Beierle et al., Alzette: a 64-bit ARX-box (feat. CRAX and TRAX)
